signals.label: Net Liquidity
signals.implication: Fed assets minus TGA/RRP drains are net expanding — a tailwind for risk-asset valuations.

signals.label: RRP Buffer
signals.implication: RRP buffer is nearly exhausted — further QT will start hitting bank reserves directly instead of being cushioned.

signals.label: Reserve Scarcity (SOFR-IORB)
signals.implication: SOFR is trading at or below IORB — reserves remain ample and repo funding is orderly.

signals.label: Financial Conditions (NFCI)
signals.implication: Financial conditions are looser than average — supportive of risk-taking.

signals.label: Credit Stress (HY OAS)
signals.implication: High-yield spreads are tight — credit markets see ample liquidity and low near-term default risk.

overall.summary: Liquidity conditions are net supportive for risk assets — plumbing, reserves, and credit are all in benign territory.

signals.label: VIX Level
signals.implication: VIX is in its normal range — no strong edge either buying or selling premium off level alone.

signals.label: VIX Term Structure
signals.implication: Curve is in steep contango — the normal, complacent state that favors carry/premium-selling strategies.

signals.label: VVIX (Vol of VIX)
signals.implication: VVIX is in a normal range — no unusual demand for crash protection beyond what VIX already implies.

signals.label: Put/Call Ratio
signals.implication: Put/call is in a normal range — no extreme positioning either way.

signals.label: Credit Cross-Check (HY OAS)
signals.implication: Credit spreads are tight — if equity vol is elevated without credit confirmation, it's more likely a technical/liquidity move that tends to mean-revert faster.

signals.label: MOVE Index (Bond Vol)
signals.implication: Rates volatility is contained — no cross-asset warning from the bond market right now.

overall.summary: Vol is broadly quiet across equity and rates markets, with no confirming credit stress — a benign backdrop, though complacency itself is worth flagging at extremes.
